title: Why Does Ice Cream Give You Brain Freeze?
description:
Why Does Ice Cream Give You Brain Freeze?
A Pip and Ray science short. Educational, not medical advice.

lines.speaker: RAY
lines.text: Pip! SLOW DOWN! You just grabbed your forehead... what happened?!

lines.speaker: PIP
lines.text: Ow ow ow! Brain freeze! That ice cream went straight to my HEAD!

lines.speaker: RAY
lines.text: But nothing touched your head! The cold is in your MOUTH! So why does your FOREHEAD hurt?!

lines.speaker: PIP
lines.text: Wait... yeah! How does ice cream... freeze my BRAIN?!

lines.speaker: RAY
lines.text: It doesn't! Your brain is perfectly warm. Watch what really happens...

lines.speaker: RAY
lines.text: Doctors' best theory: when extreme cold slams the roof of your mouth, tiny blood vessels NARROW... then quickly WIDEN again! That sudden change fires a pain signal up a huge nerve... the trigeminal nerve!

lines.speaker: PIP
lines.text: A nerve? But then... why does my FOREHEAD hurt?!

lines.speaker: RAY
lines.text: That nerve also covers your face and forehead! So your brain reads the alarm... from the wrong address. It feels the pain in your head... not your mouth!

lines.speaker: PIP
lines.text: So my brain... blamed the wrong address?!

lines.speaker: RAY
lines.text: Ha! Exactly! And the fix is easy... press your tongue on the roof of your mouth to warm it back up!

lines.speaker: PIP
lines.text: Whoa... my tongue is a tiny heater!
